newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end 110 points higher on rate relief.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end 110 points higher on rate relief.

text.p: Toronto's key equities index surged more than 1.7 percent on Wednesday as investors celebrated a decision by the U.S. central bank to hold U.S. short-term interest rates steady.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index climbed 111.30 points to end the day at 6549.04, just below the all-time high of 6557 set on June 16.

Market players widely expected the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged after a two-day committee meeting, but still breathed a sign of relief, RBC Dominion Securities investment adviser Ira Katzin said.

Investors also pushed Toronto higher in an attempt to match New York's 50-point gain on Tuesday when brokerages were shut down for the Canada Day holiday, Katzin said. "The Canadian market also played catch-up to the U.S.'s solid performance yesterday."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average also soared 73 points to 7795 on Wednesday.
A trader wondered when the TSE's recent rally would end. "I'm getting nosebleeds off this market but you can't fight the tape," he said.
All Toronto's 14 sub-indexes gained ground, led by media, heavyweight banks, utilities, pipelines and conglomerates.
Trading was modest at 82 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.2 billion). The 300 Composite Index came close but failed to break its record close of 6550.61 points on June 13.
Advancing issues edged out declining ones 483 to 448 while 277 ended steady.

In hot stocks, small oil firm Grad & Walker Energy Corp. jumped 2.35 to 13.50 and topped the most actives after Crestar Energy Inc. said it agreed to acquire Calgary, Alberta-based Grad & Walker in a C$336.2 million ($244.1 million) deal.
Crestar, also based in Calgary, offered Grad & Walker holders C$13.50 in cash or 0.509 Crestar common shares for each Grad & Walker common share.

Northern Telecom Ltd. rose 7.30 to 131.75 in heavy trading as companies continue to hunger for its services, Katzin said. Nortel's strength also boosted shares of parent firm BCE Inc., the nation's largest publicly traded firm, up 1.55 to 39.95.
